To address this gap, some authors have attempted to incorporate more elements of the child-centred approach in educational
settings, including the notions of agency and participation.
These perspectives view children as active participants and
the most reliable source of information on all matters that
affect them (Mayeza, 2017). The basic principle is that considering their perspectives and allowing them to generate and
exchange their own interpretations will enhance their self-esteem
and overall welfare. Moreover, it will facilitate communication
with their peers and, collectively, foster the development of
problem-solving abilities (Gornik & Sedmak, 2021).
Although many consider this approach positive for children’s
overall development and well-being, it is primarily a theoretical perspective. It serves as a general guiding principle that
requires adaptation for practical implementation. The evidence
and practical guidelines for its implementation are still insufficiently developed
